To address these issues, this research proposes an automated system that utilizes deep learning algorithms to classify waste items accurately. By training deep neural networks on large datasets of waste images, the system can categorize waste items into predefined classes, enabling automated sorting processes. Integration with robotic systems allows for the implementation of real-time waste sorting and processing, reducing the need for manual intervention and improving overall efficiency. The proposed approach aims to enhance waste management practices, promote recycling efforts, and contribute to environmental sustainability. Through the adoption of advanced technologies such as deep learning, this automated waste management system offers a promising solution to the challenges of modern waste management.

articleTitle: Assessment of Heart-Attack Prediction using Fuzzy Rule Based System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: This paper evaluates the prediction of heart attacks with a fuzzy rule-based system (FRBS). Since heart disease is the world's leading cause of death, precise prediction models are crucial for prevention and early intervention. With its reputation for managing imprecise and ambiguous data, fuzzy logic presents a viable method for raising prediction accuracy in medical diagnostics. In order to capture the complexity and unpredictability of cardiovascular risk variables, fuzzy rules are used in this work to investigate the creation and assessment of a fuzzy rule-based system (FRBS) for heart attack prediction. The efficacy and dependability of the FRBS in identifying those at high risk of heart attack are shown via testing and comparison with conventional prediction models. The results highlight fuzzy logic's potential to improve cardiovascular predictive analytics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Efficiency through Human-less Automation at Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: This research paper explores the functionality of temperature sensors and motion sensors for making an Arduino-based laboratory automation system. In this paper the tube lights and fans of laboratory are controlled by sensing the human presence using motion sensors. The combination of DHT 11 temperature sensor and motion sensor enables improvements in accessibility, safety, energy saving and efficiency in the laboratory environments. Four laboratories at department are automatically controlled. Additionally, DHT 11 temperature sensors sense the temperature of laboratory environment and according to that fans speed operated.

articleTitle: Disaster Management: Mobilizing Safety During Calamity
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Natural disasters are a big threat to people's lives, causing a lot of harm. One major problem in dealing with disasters is that there's often a communication issue between people stuck in dangerous situations and the teams trying to rescue them. This lack of communication makes it hard for rescuers to do their job quickly and effectively because they don't know how many people are trapped or where they are. On top of that, many people in disaster-prone areas don't know how to prepare for emergencies, making the impact of disasters even worse. To address these challenges, this paper describes a system, which includes all in one mobile application for diverse civilians which offers user-friendly interface, operability throughout India, anti-disaster literacy with multi-language feature for a broader audience, and track, store & keep appending their live locations in secure database after some interval of time. Additionally, a machine learning based system which will count trapped civilians’ frequency and mark hotspot (disaster prone) regions using civilian's live locations & past stored locations. This project aims to rescue trapped civilians in disaster and also improve how communities get ready for and respond to disasters.

articleTitle: Design and Evolution of a Mobile Phone Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Here, the work focuses on the evolution and the design of a mobile phone detector, which has the ability to pick up both outgoing and incoming mobile phone signals. This compact, pocket-sized mobile transmission detector has a range of 1.5 meters to detect the presence of the active mobile cell phone. Because of this technique, it might be helpful in prohibiting the usage of cell phones in the exam rooms, private spaces, gas stations, etc. Moreover, some illegal practices like spying, unauthorized video transmission can also be easily detected by this. The circuit surely can identify both the incoming and the outgoing calls, SMS messages, and WhatsApp messages, also while the phone is in quite mode or do not disturb mode. When the bug senses an active mobile phone's radio frequency (RF) transmission, it begins to emit an alarm-like beep sound and blinks its light-emitting diode (LED). Up till the signal transmission is stopped, the alarm sounds.

articleTitle: Automated Soil Profile Analysis Using Optical Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Soil plays a vital role in the environmental cycle, particularly in agriculture, where it is essential for sustaining human life by maintaining adequate food production. The quality of soil is crucial in this context, as it contains inorganic material, organic matter, minerals, and microorganisms necessary for plant growth. However, human activities increasingly pollute the soil, threatening its quality. To enhance soil quality, testing is vital. Traditional soil testing methods are often time-consuming and expensive. To address these challenges, this study proposes an automated soil profile analyzer that assesses soil profile for agricultural purposes based on soil color.This automated soil profile analyzer uses an optical sensor to detect soil color through RGB values. The system integrates an optical module with an Arduino board, creating a database of RGB values corresponding to different color chips in the Munsell soil chart. When analyzing an unknown soil sample, its RGB values are compared to the database in a Python environment. The results provide the Munsell color code for the sample, allowing determination of soil profile.

articleTitle: Detection of Objects to Assist Individuals with Visual Impaired Using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Navigating the world with visual impairments presents significant challenges. This project aims to develop a real-time object detection system to empower individuals with visual impairments, enhancing their mobility and independence. By harnessing the power of computer vision and machine learning, the system will employ object detection algorithms to identify and classify objects in the user's environment. This information will then be relayed through intuitive audio feedback, enabling users to perceive and interact with their surroundings more effectively. The project will encompass the exploration and evaluation of various state-of-the-art object detection algorithms, ultimately integrating the most effective solution into a comprehensive and user-friendly system

articleTitle: Enhanced Geospatial Raster Data Protection: Harnessing Chaos Maps and DNA Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Securing the transmission of digital images in geospatial data is vital, given its sensitive nature and diverse applications. Proper encryption and authentication scheme to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the data and prevent unauthorized access. This proposed work investigates the approach in cryptography by integrating chaos mapping with DNA computing for creating robust image encryption system using Chirikov map and Chebyshiv Map. The research proposes a secure encryption framework for digital images using a security function, focusing on a disease detection module based on chaotic systems and DNA inspired techniques to generate the encryption key and image scrambling for the robustness of the encryption. Furthermore, the study combines chaos theory with DNA computing in encrypting data to secure maximum security and efficiency.

articleTitle: Intelligent Application for Dog Emotion Detection using EfficientNet-B0
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The present research paper introduces an innovative methodology for classifying canine emotions by employing the EfficientNet-B0 algorithm. The recognition of emotions by animals, specifically canines, is a crucial factor in comprehending their conduct and improving the quality of human-animal relationships. This research study addresses the task of precise dog emotion recognition, like happy, sad, angry, relaxed. In this study, the model, fine-tuned, is used to cover different emotions in dogs and has a classification accuracy of 89%, thus showing its potential to recognize emotions like anger, happiness, relaxation and sadness among dogs. The Efficient net- B0 model is meticulously trained on an augmented dataset known as Stanford’s Dog Emotion dataset, which consists of images of dogs with labels indicating their emotional state: angry, happy, relaxed, or sad. Metrics that show constant performance, such as accuracy, loss, AUC, and precision when viewed visually, show consistent performance. According to the data, EfficientNet-B0 is good at correctly detecting dogs' emotions, which could be useful in veterinary care, animal behavior research, and studies of how people interact with animals.

articleTitle: Kernel-Level Semantic Search with Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Various types of knowledge exist across individuals, processes, and tools. The chief objective of Knowledge Graph (KG) is to aggregate the data into graph format, ensuring that it remains manageable, non-corrupted, scalable, and easily discoverable.At its core, a KG is a structure where each node represents real-world entities and edges logically depict the relationships between the nodes. The graph can be directed or un-directed, depending on the organization’s needs. Our approach involves a directed graph that also includes backward edges!The end objective of KG is to operationalize Knowledge (a piece of information) at the kernel level and make it available to users when they feed specific queries to the graph. The output should be the most relevant and concise response available, neither too lengthy nor too brief.

articleTitle: Federated Learning Approach for Social Media Sentiment Analysis: Analyzing Public Opinion
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: This paper examines how federated learning can be applied to social media sentiment analysis, focusing on public opinion across various online platforms. By using federated learning, we combine sentiment analysis models from multiple sources while maintaining data privacy and security. Our experiments show that federated learning successfully captures dynamic sentiment trends across different social media sites. The findings offer valuable insights into public opinion, benefiting businesses, policymakers, and researchers. Future research will explore advanced federated learning techniques, optimize model architectures, include multimodal data, evaluate performance across different demographics and languages, and address scalability for large datasets. This study lays the groundwork for using federated learning in social media sentiment analysis and advancing the understanding of public sentiment in the digital era.

articleTitle: Analysis on Crop Yield Prediction using various Ensemble Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Agriculture is a crucial facet of human existence as it fulfils the primary and fundamental requirement of sustenance, namely food. Therefore, it is incumbent upon us, as human beings, to cultivate and enhance our agricultural methodologies. Crop Yield Prediction is a method that enables farmers to determine the most suitable crops to produce in specific seasons based on historical data, prior to harvesting. This research examines the prediction of crop productivity in three distinct states of India. The states are Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha. We employ many ensemble methods, namely Random Forest, XGB Regression, and Stacking Regression, in which we combine Random Forest and XGB Regression. Next, compute the results by evaluating L1 and L2 using LASSO and Ridge Regression. Ultimately, XGB Regression yields a more precise outcome in comparison to the other two methods.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Improving DR Diagnosis Accuracy with Deep Learning Using Adjudicated Grading
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Globally, diabetic retinopathy, or DR, is one of the main causes of blindness. The effectiveness of deep learning models in diagnosing DR from retinal fundus images is hindered by inconsistencies in training data quality. This study addresses this issue by integrating adjudicated grading, a process involving independent assessments of image sets by trained readers with discrepancies resolved by an expert adjudicator. This approach is evaluated using the Messidor 2 dataset, comprising 1,200 retinal images with adjudicated grades for DR and diabetic macular edema (DME). The results show significant improvements in model accuracy,achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.95 for DR diagnosis and 0.91 for DME detection. This research highlights the potential of combining adjudicated grading and deep learning models to enhance the precision of DR diagnosis and screening, with broad implications for public health and healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Home Automation System By Android Application And Voice Control
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: In home automation, integrating Arduino and Android technology has paved the way for sophisticated yet user-friendly solutions. This paper presents a detailed guide on building a do-it-yourself home appliance control system using Arduino and an Android app. The system allows users to control various home appliances, including lights and fans, from their smartphones. Central to the system is the Arduino Nano, serving as the brain, and the HC-05 Bluetooth module for wireless communication with the Android application. A 4-channel relay module is used for appliance control, and a 5-volt, 2-ampere power adapter provides the necessary power. The paper discusses the integration of the EEPROM library into the Arduino code to maintain load statuses across power cycles. The code also utilizes the SoftwareSerial library to enable communication with the Bluetooth module without detaching it during code upload. The Android app, developed using the MIT App Inventor, features buttons for load control, a Bluetooth connection button, and labels for displaying load and power statuses. Voice control functionality is implemented using speech recognition, enhancing accessibility and hands-free operation.The paper concludes with a discussion of the energy-saving and convenience benefits of home automation. It encourages enthusiasts to explore further enhancements and expand the system’s capabilities to create a fully automated smart home. Overall, the combination of Arduino and Android technology offers a comprehensive home automation solution, enabling users to control their appliances effortlessly through both voice and physical controls.

articleTitle: Adaptive Load Balancing Strategies for Reducing System Failures in Network Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: WSN are now essential components of contemporary network infrastructures, providing instantaneous data collection and environmental surveillance in diverse domains. Nevertheless, these networks encounter substantial obstacles such as congestion, system failures, and inefficient energy usage. Adaptive load balancing strategies are essential for enhancing network performance and resilience in order to tackle these issues. This study introduces a new method that utilizes density-based cluster head selection algorithms to enhance load balancing, effective data aggregation, routing, and energy management in wireless sensor networks (WSN). The proposed adaptive load balancing strategy employs an advanced clustering algorithm that chooses cluster heads based on both node density and residual energy, guaranteeing effective network organization and communication. This method employs adaptive mechanisms to accommodate fluctuations in network conditions, ensuring equitable distribution of traffic throughout the network and mitigating the potential for system failures caused by excessive load. The proposed strategy shows substantial enhancements in energy efficiency and network lifespan when compared to conventional density-based cluster head selection methods, as evidenced by experimental evaluations. The findings demonstrate that our methodology results in decreased energy usage and enhanced energy retention within the network. The results indicate that the proposed method exhibits lower energy consumption (170 units) compared to density-based cluster head selection (299 units), while also maintaining higher remaining energy levels (13,930 units) compared to the traditional approach (13,801 units). The findings emphasize the effectiveness of the adaptive load balancing strategy in prolonging the lifespan of WSN and decreasing the likelihood of system failures.

articleTitle: Leveraging BERT for Tailored Movie Suggestions: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The Primary aim is to enhance the development of personalised movie suggestions by developing a content-based movie recommender system and offering consumers a well-chosen selection that aligns with their individual cinematic tastes. The study explores the complexities of content-based recommendation with the goal of revealing hidden patterns in the movie data and providing a more thorough, nuanced understanding of user preferences using efficient machine learning algorithms and NLP models such as BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Binary Sequence Detector with Functional Verification, Synthesis, PnR and STA using open-source EDA tool
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The study focuses on developing a VLSI-based Binary Sequence Detector using open-source Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. It emphasizes the synthesis, PnR and STA of the sequence detector. Key goals include designing and implementing a binary sequence detector in Verilog, incorporating functional verification, synthesis, placement and routing, and static timing analysis (STA) through open-source EDA tools. Through a thorough literature review, reversible sequential circuit construction methods using FPGAs are explored, highlighting the effectiveness of open-source tools. Diverse methodologies for high-speed sequence detectors in Verilog are examined, emphasizing flexibility, efficiency, and scalability.

articleTitle: ML Based Ultra Processed Food Categorization with Limited Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Ultra processed foods have permeated modern diets, raising concerns about their health implications. This study introduces a pioneering approach utilizing ML algorithms notably Random Forest and XGBoost, to analyze packaged food products and categorize them based on their healthiness levels. Data sourced from users included extensive nutritional information of various packaged food items. Leveraging the collected data from our responses Random Forest, XGBoost and Naive Bayes Classifiers were implemented to classify the products into the categories defined by Nutri-Score FOP Labelling system which classifies the food products into 5 categories from A (being most preferable) TO E (being worst preferable) based on the score they achieve depending on their nutritional content. We are able to obtain valuable insights for consumers and regulatory bodies facilitating informed dietary choices and addressing the challenges faced with awareness of ultra-processed foods and their consumption.

articleTitle: Decentralized Fund Management System for Indian Temples Powered by Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: This research provides a proposal to integrate blockchain technology with a web application to come up with a solution for the fund management issues that the temples face. The main purpose of the research is to solve the problems of transparency, corruption and trust amidst donors and authorities of temple. Enabling the combination of a database management arrangement and a user-friendly website, a private blockchain was developed. The website is powered by smart contracts and serves as a solution that is capable of making fund operations accountable and visible. The outcomes of using this solution showed improvement in transparency, less corruption and increase of trust among donors. The temple authorities became more answerable and efficient as donors observed the movement of the donations in real time. This study gives a possible solution for temples to get the trust of their members back in order to ensure that the donations are properly implemented and a generation of cultural heritage is conserved.

articleTitle: Travel With Generator AI: A Novel Approach to Itinerary Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The usual problems that arise are in the efficiency of itinerary planning of the Travelers. The problem with all travel options and destinations is the challenge of organizing a personal itinerary according to personal preferences, constraints, and interests. Traditional methods of itinerary planning are both inflexible and time-consuming, which produces many generic recommendations that do not take into consideration the preferences of the travelers or address the comprehensive travel experience. These problems are solved by our app: it incorporates user preferences into the itinerary generation, allowing the input of user preferences by the users. Machine learning algorithms then analyze these preferences and generate personalized recommendations based on them. This way, each itinerary is specifically tailored to your needs, making the experience that much more enjoyable and fulfilling.

articleTitle: PredatorSense-Wildlife Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: This system explores the transformative applications of machine learning, specifically deep learning, in the domain of wildlife detection and alerting. It addresses two crucial domains: the automatic detection of animals in human-inhabited areas and the effective monitoring and protection of wild animals near forest boundaries. In human-inhabited areas, the presence of animals straying into densely populated regions poses significant security and safety challenges. This system provides valuable insights into the complexities of transfer learning, shedding light on the challenges encountered when adapting models trained on Google Open Images datasets in [2] to real-world deployment scenarios. Shifting its focus to wildlife conservation and protection near forest boundaries, this system underscores the critical need for effective monitoring. Efficient deep learning techniques enable the system to provide timely and reliable alerts, even in remote sensing areas where standard communication technologies may falter.It offers cost-effective solutions, mitigating the hardware implementation costs compared to existing systems [3], [4]. Our system demonstrates an 4.65% improvement over [1], [2] by effectively utilizing SSD MobileNet model for automatic animal detection addressing challenges in transfer learning and offering cost-effective solutions.

articleTitle: Iris Liveness detection using SIFT, SURF and SVM with Quality Metrics for Biometric Authentication
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Iris recognition technology has become increasingly popular in applications involving biometric security because of its precision and uniqueness. These systems are vulnerable to fraudulent attacks, in which counterfeit iris samples are used to spoof the verification process. To address this issue, various methods for detecting iris authenticity have been developed to differentiate legitimate and counterfeit iris images. This paper presents a methodology for identifying iris Liveness using a Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), Speeded Up Robust Features (SURF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) with quality Metrics. Our approach includes pre-processing iris images, extracting distinguishing characteristics using SIFT and SURF techniques, and SVM for classification. The results of experiments conducted on a standard Clarkson dataset 2017 and CASIA-Iris-Thousand, demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving remarkable precision in distinguishing between authentic and counterfeit iris images. This study contributes to the development of iris liveness detection technology and demonstrates the potential for enhancing the security of biometric verification systems.

articleTitle: PromptArt: AI-Powered Image Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Conventional picture creation requests noteworthy ability and labor, frequently constraining inventive expression to a select gather of capable specialists. This restrictiveness makes obstructions for amateurs and devotees, smothering differing qualities and advancement in visual craftsmanship. Whereas cutting-edge AI frameworks guarantee computerized picture amalgamation, they habitually battle to decipher nuanced printed prompts precisely, driving client disappointment when the coming about pictures don’t meet desires. PromptArt addresses these challenges by leveraging Generative Ill-disposed Systems (GANs) to create high-quality pictures from literary depictions. This venture aims to democratize the inventive handle, engaging people of all skill levels to make personalized pictures easily. PromptArt’s dual-stage GAN design first translates textual prompts into starting picture drafts and after that refines these drafts to improve quality and coherence, guaranteeing that the visual yields closely adjust with the client eagerly. With a user-friendly interface, PromptArt makes it simple for clients to input printed depictions and get high-quality visual representations. This openness changes the imaginative preparation, permitting more individuals to lock in in visual craftsmanship creation and contributing to a more different and inventive social scene. This paper investigates the engineering plan and execution of PromptArt, specifying its strategies and comes about. We moreover talk about the broader suggestions of democratizing picture creation, highlighting how PromptArt can cultivate more prominent imagination, collaboration, and social engagement, revolutionizing the way we make and connect with visual craftsmanship.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Breast Cancer Ternary-Class Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the chronic illnesses that can occur in human beings irrespective of their gender. Usually, women are the ones mostly affected who are infrequently men. The stage of breast cancer has a significant impact on the treatment therapy. Invasive breast cancer refers to the treatable stage of the disease. During the invasive phase, the malignant cells are limited to the smallest area of the breast. As a result, it is challenging to diagnose breast cancer when it is aggressive. Stage-I, Stage-II, and Stage-III belong to the invasive phase of cancer. When breast cancer is discovered at these stages, treating the patient by the cancer's stage is simple. Machine learning techniques allow us to predict, and detect cancer, and help reveal the cancer stages during an invasive phase.The study tackles several major challenges in the field of breast cancer prediction, such as the difficulties in integrating datasets and missing data, the necessity of precise ternary classification to predict the stages of breast cancer, and the significance of assessing classifier performance using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. This paper presents a machine learning model to predict the stages of breast cancer and stage predictions belonging to the ternary classification as well as explores the importance of the confusion matrix. This work uses the Multinomial Logistic Regression machine learning technique to predict the ternary classification. The breast cancer data is used for the simulation. The performance of the simulation is evaluated in accuracy and precision. This technique predicts stages of breast cancer with 66% accuracy and 70.33% precision by using a confusion matrix.

articleTitle: Predicting Employee Performance using Machine Learning to Enhance Workforce Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop a machine learning model that utilizes historical employee data to predict future performance within organizational contexts. To achieve this, employees are categorized into three distinct groups: high performers, moderate performers, and low performers. The objective is to use this data to enhance talent management and decision-making in organizations. Building the machine learning model involves addressing challenges such as data quality, bias, and interpretability. Compared to current methods, anticipated outcomes involve achieving higher levels of accuracy, computational complexity, and adaptability. However, ethical considerations, including fairness and transparency, remain essential to this study. Hence, the aim of this study is to offer a flexible and forward-looking approach that adapts to changing organizational dynamics, meeting companies' needs for innovative approaches to workforce management.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Linear Regression, Random Forest Regressor and LSTM for Stock Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Stock price prediction is an important topic of research in financial markets and many machine learning algorithms are used to estimate future stock prices. This study compares three prominent stock price prediction algorithms: Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). The main objective of the research is to assess these algorithms' predictive ability using R-squared (R2), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) metrics. The study uses historical data from ten S&P 500 and ten NIFTY 50 stocks to represent a wide range of industries and market circumstances. This data is used to train and test each algorithm, and the evaluation criteria indicated above are used to determine each method’s performance. The study’s findings offer an insight into the ability of Linear Regression, Random Forest, and LSTM models in predicting stock values across markets and sectors.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Methods Towards Effective Transportation based Predictive Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Transportation is the backbone for every industry with the rise in having everything at our doorstep. Transportation is a significant domain as it is required for transferring goods to and fro from one place to another. Machine Learning is gaining a lot of popularity in recent times because of its immeasurable power of problem solving. Regressive methods that are a domain of machine learning algorithms have been proven to be successful because they have a strong mathematical foundation and can be compared against other approaches to find out which approach is the most compatible to perform on the dataset to give the finest result. By conducting a comparative analysis of error metrics, including Confusion Matrix, Accuracy, Precision, Recall we attempt to evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the model. This study aims to contribute to the betterment of predictive models in a transportation dataset and offers insights into the limitations of Machine Learning algorithms on the selected model through which we find that Logistic regression works best on our model with an accuracy of 0.65 and Lasso was the most unfit regression for our dataset.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: GestureX: Text Generation based on the Gesture Identified using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Technology has made remarkable strides, and it is crucial to use new technologies for the benefit of those who are hard of hearing. These people faces many issues in communication. To address this issue system is proposed leverages cutting-edge tools like MediaPipe and TensorFlow to enhance communication. The proposed system is able to understand sign language in real-time, offering a simple and effective solution. The key challenge it tackles is the variability of sign language, which can be influenced by factors like lighting and signing style. To address this a smart computer model using LSTM, has been developed to ensure accurate gesture recognition and through that sign language interpretation. This technique designed has the potential to significantly improve the lives of those with hearing difficulties, making socializing, learning, and conversing much easier for them.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of MAC Protocols for Node Density in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: A wireless sensor network is a group of various forms of nodes that are arranged at random around the sensor area. In WSNs, certain nodes operate as source nodes, monitoring factors from the nearby area, while one node acts as a sink node, collecting information from source nodes. Clustering, sectoring, and sleep-active mechanism are just some of the different methods used in WSNs to provide reliable transmission of information between one point to another. The efficiency of wireless sensor networks is determined by their quality of services, or QoS, which includes factors like packet delivery ratio, energy, throughput, delay etc. Transferring information from one end to the other requires the use of mac protocols and routing. Routing protocols are used to determine the shortest path between the sending and receiving nodes, while the MAC protocol ensures reliable data transfer via communication channels between nodes. In this paper, we analyzed the efficacy of multiple MAC protocols with various QoS for different node densities. This will assist inventors in the future with analysis. The CSMA protocol performs effectively for all network QoS standards.

articleTitle: Improved ECG Lead Detection and Classification using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an essential tool in diagnosing heart conditions, providing critical insights through its 12 individual leads. Accurate analysis of these leads is vital for a precise diagnosis. Traditionally, ECG analysis has predominantly focused on signal-based methodologies. However, integrating image analysis of ECGs alongside signal analysis can significantly enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. To explore this integration, we at Emprotek Software Solutions conducted an experiment utilizing YOLOv8, a stateof-the-art object detection model, trained over 100 epochs to detect ECG leads from ECG report images effectively. Our experimentation utilized the "ECG Images Dataset for Cardiac Patients," a comprehensive collection of ECG images representative of various cardiac conditions. The performance metrics obtained from our model are impressive, with a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.992, recall (R) of 1, mAP at 50% IoU (mAP50) of 0.995, and mAP at 50-95% IoU (mAP50-95) of 0.756. These results demonstrate a high degree of accuracy and consistency, aligning well with existing literature in the field of ECG analysis. Furthermore, our study highlights the potential for advanced image analysis techniques to complement traditional signal-based approaches, paving the way for more robust and comprehensive ECG diagnostics. The promising outcomes from our experimentation underscore the importance of continued research and development in this hybrid analysis domain, aiming to enhance the precision and reliability of cardiac health assessments.

articleTitle: Facial Image Generation using fully trained Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Recent advancements in facial image generation have been significant. However, many existing methods are constrained to generating face images solely from random noise, lacking the capability to synthesize images based on specific features. In this work, the issue of face synthesis from features is mapped, trying to produce facial images that have unique features that match pre-specified criteria. In order to accomplish this goal, this research presents new techniques for generating attribute-aware face images using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which include Conditional GAN (CGAN), Wasserstein GAN (WGAN), and Deep Convolutional GAN (DCGAN).This paper’s method starts by converting the input text into an array of its features and then mapped with GAN. Subsequently, three stacked generators are utilized to produce face images of resolutions 64×64, 128×128, and 256×256, respectively, using characteristic traits as the input. Furthermore, a proposed image-attribute matching loss is made to improve the relation between the input vector with the generated images. Prolonged testing on the CelebA dataset confirms the efficacy of the CGAN, WGAN, and DCGAN methods presented in this work. This paper shows the comparison of CGAN, DCGAN and WGAN based on various performance evaluation parameters such as Inception score, Generator’s loss and Discriminators loss for a particular number of training epochs.

articleTitle: Review on Blockchain and Fake product identification using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The proliferation of fake goods has had a significant effect on the industrial sector in recent years. According to the research, the number of occurrences involving bogus products has increased recently, which is hurting the company's reputation, earnings, and sales. Users must have a method to identify if a product is real or false. The blockchain facilitates more transparent and easy transactions. Data security is increased by blockchain technology because once a block is formed, it cannot be changed or altered—even if there is just one alteration that affects the hash value. This essay offers a thorough analysis of the literature on the topics of blockchain, its applications, how it operates, and how it might be used to detect counterfeit goods. The goal is to look at the different types of fraud and the effects they have., this paper guides developers to design and evaluate consensus mechanism in blockchain systems.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Fetal Skull Anomalies using Web-Based Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Congenital fetal anomalies occur between 2-3 % of pregnancies globally. Approximately 20 % of anomalies have a genetic issue, including those caused by underlying chromosomal abnormalites or an individual gene defect. Mainly there are 2 types of fetal anomalies structural anomalies and functional anomalies, structural anomalies influence the growing baby’s heart, kidneys, lungs, limbs and facial features and functional anomalies influence the working of an organ or system, such as the brain.This research proposes an approach to improve quality of prenatal diagnosis for early detection of fetal anomalies. This paper proposed a convolutional neural network-based deep learning technique to identify Cloverleaf anomaly in the developing skull using information from ultrasound images and the Transfer Learning method. Ultrasound data is used to compare between different architectures VGG16, ResNet50, MobileNet-v2 and Proposed Algorithm to find the optimal CNN. Experimental results based on Transfer Learning indicated that the Proposed Algorithm outperformed the pre-trained CNN models (MobileNet-v2, ResNet50, and VGG16). Additionally, created the Flask web application, which provides a unified platform for detecting prenatal anomalies. The app, with its user-friendly design and prediction capabilities, is a valuable resource for medical experts and expectant parents looking for accurate prenatal diagnoses. The proposed model might be useful for early detection of prenatal skull anomalies.

articleTitle: The Low-RCS Drone: A Compact, Cost-Effective Covert Drone for Efficient Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: This paper introduces a cost-effective covert drone prototype designed to evade detection in an era of heightened surveillance. Inspired by ancient texts like the Vaimānika Shāstra, the project integrates historical knowledge with modern technology, achieving a 60-70% reduction in manufacturing costs through innovative engineering. The drone features a single BLDC motor powered by a commercially available drone battery, housed in a radar-evading aerodynamic structure. Compact and lightweight, it measures under 30 cm and weighs less than 500 grams, making it easily portable. Mathematical formulations show that the torus-shaped object exhibits significantly lower Radar Cross Section (RCS) at different angles compared to other systems, offering potential benefits for military applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Range Estimation for an Electric Vehicle Positioned on Lead Acid battery
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: In the recent few years, the growth of Electrical vehicles has increased drastically at the global level, and at the same time, there are prominent opportunities in the field of range estimation of an Electric vehicle. In today’s era, the Electric Vehicle is in rapid growth as compared to ICE-powered Vehicles. The drawback of EVs is that they do not have a 100 percent accuracy when it comes to depicting the range which leads to inconvenience. One of the most significant problems faced by numerous users of electric vehicles is the accuracy of the range estimation on their EVs. Environmental factors affecting battery performance, especially in EVs with lead-acid batteries, aggravate this problem. Basically, it can be simplified as calculating the accurate range of an EV while considering external factors like road conditions and the change in the weight of the vehicle simultaneously. To improve range precision and give drivers the confidence to rely on more precise estimations for their electric travels, a thorough comprehension and analysis of these elements is necessary. These issues should be addressed to ease the shift to electric vehicles. The proposed study can be of utmost usefulness in increasing the efficiency of any vehicle to overcome the problem.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Classifiers for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: In today’s cybersecurity landscape, the continuous evolution and diversification of malware present a significant threat, necessitating its effective detection and classification. With malware types becoming more sophisticated, the demand for advanced detection techniques is paramount. The detection and classification of malware constitutes a critical challenge, necessitating the deployment of sophisticated machine learning (ML) techniques. This study proposes a methodology that leverages a variety of machine learning (ML) models, including Naive Bayes, Decision Trees, Extra Trees, Random Forest, AdaBoost, Gradient Boost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Support Vector Machines, fine-tuned for optimal performance. Conducting a comprehensive performance analysis across binary, 4-class, and 16-class classification tasks on the extensive CIC-Malmem2022 dataset, this research aims to identify the most effective classifier for malware detection and classification. This study emphasizes LightGBM’s superiority over other classifiers due to its strong performance with categorical features and large datasets. This highlights its potential to bolster cybersecurity by enhancing malware detection and optimizing ML classifiers against evolving threats.

articleTitle: Detecting Plant Diseases Utilizing a Convolutional Neural Network and Transfer-Learning Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Timely detection of diseases in plants significantly impacts the production of high-quality and abundant grains. These precision techniques have shown impressive results in plant leaf-based image classification. This paper uses the Convolutional Neural Network and Transfer-Learning application EfficientNetB7 to identify fresh and diseased leaves. Various parameters such as accuracy, block size, dropouts, loss, and time required for epochs were incorporated to appraise the model performance. This paper consists of several phases Implementation, i.e., creation of datasets, feature extraction, and training the classifier. Image dataset from Kaggle village plant datasets used for training and testing which contains several fresh and diseased leaves images. The deep CNN model is promising accurate results in identifying diseases has a notable impact on effective disease identification and could potentially enable disease detection in agricultural systems in real time. EfficientNetB7 compared to other Transfer-Learning applications such as ResNet, Inceptions, MobileNet, and DenseNet has a smaller number of parameters and achieved 99.89% performance accuracy is also higher than others.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Quantum Algorithms: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Quantum computing is a rapidly growing field. Quantum algorithms play a significant role and have applications in cryptography, machine learning, optimization, and computational issues [1][2]. They quantum features like entanglement and superposition that help carryout tasks that would be difficult for a classical computer. More Interest has been developed in Quantum algorithms due to their ability to solve specific computational problems quicker than that in classical algorithms [3]. These algorithms use fundamentals of quantum physics to carryout calculations quickly and effectively than traditional algorithms. Here in-depth analysis of quantum algorithms and classical algorithms is done by looking at the time and space complexity of quantum and classical algorithms including their capacity to tackle specific types of issues.First, we conduct a general comparison of Classical and Quantum Algorithm along with Background and motivation. We also discuss Simon's algorithm first and then Grover's algorithm in depth and their comparison with few other algorithms in a table format [5][6][7][8]. We also cover some recent advancements, Quantum supremacy, Post-Quantum Cryptography, 8 Quantum Artificial Intelligence, Hybrid Quantum-Classical Algorithms and few other important parameters. We also discuss the plausible impact of quantum algorithms on cybersecurity and cryptography [13][9]. Overall, this comparative study shows the uses and challenges involved in implementing quantum algorithms while offering an overview of quantum algorithms. We conclude by the fundamental ideas of quantum algorithms. Adding to this we also discuss the challenges and limitations of using quantum algorithms in practically. At the end, we provide a summary of the primary findings from this comparative study of Quantum and classical algorithms.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Energy Demand Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Increasing energy demand necessitates efficient management strategies to balance the energy demand-supply grid effectively. The research focuses on integrating energy demand forecasting approaches using regression models into building management systems. The research uses a comprehensive dataset spanning 2016 to 2018, including numerous measurements and observations on power use in buildings and time-series meteorological factors. Several regression models, including the Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Ridge, Lasso, and Gradient Boosting regressors, are used and compared. Each model's effectiveness is evaluated using performance indicators such as the R-squared (R2) score and Mean Squared Error (MSE). SVM emerges as the best option, with the highest R2 score and lowest MSE. Altogether, by integrating these forecasting models, real-time operations can optimize energy consumption management and improve prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Frequency Regulation of Power System using TID Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: This work examines the effectiveness of the tilt integral derivative (TID) controller for load frequency control (LFC) in a two-area power system. Several contemporary strategies are used to put into practice a stabilizing controller. A detailed investigation of the LFC issue in a power system with two power generating units as well as the dynamic performance of LFC through the application of optimization techniques has been developed. This paper proposes a TID control mechanism for suppressing oscillation. Recently developed methods are used to determine the appropriate controller parameters. The response of different parameters is obtained with the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: BloodBond: Optimising Blood Bank System through a Comprehensive Smart Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: In densely populated areas like Mumbai, the challenge of efficiently managing blood donations is critical. The gap between available donors and the urgent need for various blood types, especially in emergencies and for chronic conditions, necessitates a robust solution. Online Blood Bank Management System innovatively addresses this need, revolutionizing the blood donation and distribution process. The system enhances accessibility with a locality search feature, allowing donors to easily find and participate in nearby blood drives. It simplifies donor registration and donation management and includes educational resources. Hospitals and blood banks benefit from a dashboard for organizing donation events, monitoring blood stock, and managing blood group requests. The key contribution of this research paper is the Emergency Blood Request Donor Notification system, which allows hospitals to quickly alert potential donors in urgent situations. Furthermore, the integration of the Donor Retention Model, a machine learning tool, predicts the likelihood of donors becoming long-term, dedicated contributors. This model has demonstrated an impressive 78.30 % accuracy in identifying potential dedicated donors, crucial for patients requiring consistent blood supplies.

articleTitle: Visionize: Text To Image Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Visionize is presented as an innovative platform that introduces a cutting-edge text-to-image model with the potential to redefine communication and idea expression within the digital domain. This tool seamlessly translates textual descriptions into captivating images, thereby extending the boundaries of creativity and enhancing communication clarity. The streamlined work-flow facilitates the visualization of ideas without necessitating specialized design skills or software expertise. It serves as a solution applicable across various domains, including the creation of engaging social media posts, presentations, and the illustration of complex concepts. Its implementation represents a significant advancement in transforming textual input into visually compelling outputs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Parking Efficiency and Mobility with IR-based Smart Parking Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Urban mobility is severely hampered by the growing trend of urbanization and the population growth of vehicles, especially regarding parking spaces in crowded, busy areas. The suggested system uses cutting-edge technology like wireless communication, data analytics, and the Internet of Things to improve parking space utilization. With a more user-friendly user interface, this strategy seeks to improve urban transportation and reduce traffic. The "Smart Parking Management System" that is being suggested uses sensor nodes that are placed strategically across parking lots to collect data in real-time about parking spaces that are available and those that are occupied. Through communication between these sensors and a microcontroller, a network is created that continuously checks and updates the status of parking spaces. Users can access this information through a Telegram bot to remotely identify and reserve available parking spaces. The system creates a sustainable and user-friendly urban environment by streamlining traffic and allocating parking spaces optimally.

articleTitle: Denoising of Multiview Images to 3D Point Cloud Visualization using VisualSfM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Preserving our diverse cultural heritage for the future relies heavily on advanced 2D to 3D technologies. These cutting-edge tools are invaluable for documenting, recovering, and presenting tangible and intangible aspects of our heritage. Through these technological innovations, we ensure that the richness of our cultural legacy is not only preserved but also presented dynamically and accessible for future generations. To preserve heritage scenes, 2D smartphone/DSLR and 3D LiDAR cameras can capture Multiview images and visualize 3D of a scene in MeshLab using Structure from Motion workflow. However, 3D LiDAR sensors consume more power and can only capture scenes up to a certain distance. To address these issues, 2D smartphone cameras/DSLR cameras can be used. However, smartphone 2D cameras tend to exhibit more noise due to their smaller aperture and sensor size as compared to DSLR cameras. The Multiview 2D images of Chandramouleshwara Temple in Hubli, a 900-year-old Temple dedicated to the Hindu God Shiva, were captured using a Samsung mobile phone. The synthetically generated noisy images are denoised using NLM and DnCNN algorithms. The denoised images and ground truth images are compared in terms of SSIM and PSNR as image restoration performance parameters. It is observed that as the noise level increases in images, the SSIM and PSNR values are decreasing. However, the results obtained by NLM algorithm is outperformed in terms of PSNR by 4.31dB and SSIM by 0.415 compared to pre-trained DnCNN model in denoising of noisy Multiview images. The denoised Multiview images are then passed through Structure from Motion (SfM) workflow for feature correspondence, camera intrinsic/extrinsic estimation, and depth estimation using triangulation, followed by bundle adjustment to reduce reprojection error. The 3D point cloud of a denoised Multiview images is visualized in VisualSfM.

articleTitle: AI Bedtime Storyteller using Chatgpt Prompt
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The emergence of AI-powered bedtime story tellers, exemplified by ChatGPT, signifies a transformative intersection of technology and tradition. This abstract provides an overview of the concept and implications of such innovative systems. In an increasingly digital age, AI bedtime story tellers serve as remarkable companions for nurturing creativity, imagination, and language development in children. These systems leverage state-of-the-art natural language processing and machine learning techniques to generate personalized, engaging narratives tailored to individual preferences. This explores the methodology behind developing AI bedtime story tellers, encompassing data collection, model selection, fine-tuning, and user interaction. It delves into the potential educational benefits, including cognitive engagement and accessibility, while acknowledging the need for robust privacy and security measures, particularly in child-focused applications. Its envisioning enhanced personalization, interactivity, and integration with emerging technologies such as augmented reality. It emphasizes the potential for collaborative storytelling and parental involvement, fostering a rich ecosystem for family engagement and childhood development.

articleTitle: VoltGuard FemmeSecure
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The primary objective of this research is to enhance women's safety through the application of electric shock technology. The smart glove, designed as an electroshock weapon, utilizes a low current, high voltage electric discharge to override muscle triggering mechanisms and deliver an electric shock. Drawing inspiration from the electric mosquito bat, the key concept is incorporated into the glove, specifically through a knuckle fixture. The generation of alternating high voltage current is facilitated by a step-up transformer, while an oscillator and resonant circuit contribute to the overall functionality. The power source may consist of one or more batteries. The effectiveness of the output current upon contact with the target is influenced by various factors, including internal circuitry, skin type, target resistance, moisture levels, the type of clothing worn, the electric shock weapon employed, and the condition of the batteries.

articleTitle: Design of Smart Parking System using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Increasing urbanization has increased load on the city roads, traffic and parking systems. It is essential to leverage Information Communication Technologies (ICT) to enhance traffic and parking system services in an urban area. With available hardware components and software platform researchers are exploring to build effective solutions to resolve citizen problems. The present paper uses available off the shelf component to build a smart parking system. A tripod approach was used. Such a smart parking system involves user management, parking space management and cloud based administration. IR sensors are used for parking space occupancy detection; these sensors are connected to an Atmel AtMega microcontroller available on Arduino UNO. The information is communicated through a Wi-Fi protocol and cloud services were utilized using Blynk platform. The designed prototype is presented in this paper. The proposed model is an effective way of managing mid-sized parking spaces

articleTitle: EEG-Driven Approach to Improve Academic Performance via Auditory Brainwave Entrainment Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: As the most intelligent species, humans possess highly developed cognitive abilities facilitated by complex neural mechanisms. Our brains generate electrical signals in response to sensory inputs and experiences. Audiovisual Entrainment (AVE) techniques leverage this neuroplasticity, allowing external stimuli to modulate brain wave patterns. This approach has shown potential in addressing various neurological conditions, alleviating stress and anxiety, and enhancing cognitive performance and overall well-being. Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technologies enable direct monitoring and analysis of neural activity through non-invasive methods like Electroencephalography (EEG). EEG provides a cost-effective and practical solution for recording brain wave patterns during cognitive tasks, facilitating insights into neurophysiological processes and informing the development of targeted interventions, such as AVE.

articleTitle: Identification of Medicinal Herbs using Modified Xception Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Identifying medicinal herbs is important for traditional medicine, pharmacology, and protecting biodiversity. This paper proposes a novel way of identifying medicinal herbs from an image dataset. Different deep learning methods have been performed, including using pre-trained neural networks and creating custom models for herb recognition. A comprehensive analysis of convolutional neural network (CNN) models for medical picture recognition tasks, with an emphasis on architectures like VGG16, ResNet50, and several Xception versions has been done. After in-depth analysis, it can be concluded that the modified Xception architecture performs significantly better than the others, attaining the highest training and validation accuracies with the least amount of losses. The results provide important implications for healthcare applications by highlighting the crucial role that model design plays in improving the accuracy of medicinal image analysis. It also describes how AI-driven tools can help better identify medicinal herbs from images, leading to significant progress in the field of traditional medicines and pharmacology.

articleTitle: Data Integration in Smart Energy Meter Using Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Smart energy management systems, or SEMS, are intended to increase the efficacy and efficiency of energy use in a range of contexts, including residences, workplaces, and entire communities. These systems monitor and manage energy use in real time using cutting-edge IoT and communication protocols including GSM, Zigbee, and the Internet of Things. The use of cloud computing, which enables the central storage and analysis of enormous amounts of data, is one way to implement SEMS. Anywhere with an internet connection can access this data, which can be used to track energy consumption, pinpoint areas for development, and adjust and cut down on energy waste. In addition to improving energy efficiency, SEMS can also help reduce energy costs and contribute to a more sustainable energy future. By using advanced technologies and communication protocols, these systems can help individuals, businesses, and communities make informed decisions about their energy usage and take steps to reduce their carbon footprint.

articleTitle: Beam Prediction in Millimeter Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication has displayed potential in wireless networks as a strategy for achieving high data rates. Within mmWave communication systems, the utilization of beamforming serves to enhance signal integrity while mitigating the impact of path loss. Focusing mainly on forecasting the Angle of Arrival (AOA) by examining a dataset with factors like the distance between Transmitter and Receiver, Azimuth and Elevation Angles of Departure (AoD) and Arrival (AoA), path, and Frequency, this research delves into the use of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for beam prediction in mmWave communication systems. To precisely forecast the AOA based on historical channel state information, the proposed LSTM-based model is practically implemented using MATLAB. The outcomes of the simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the LSTM model in AOA prediction, consequently enhancing beamforming efficiency within millimeter-wave communication systems.

articleTitle: Cloud-Integrated Braking ECU with ESP Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Traditional braking systems often lack adaptability and require frequent maintenance checks. By leveraging cloud connectivity, this paper aims to enhance the safety and efficiency of automotive braking systems. Through comprehensive research and development, design of cloud-integrated braking Electronic Control Unit (ECU) with Electronic stability program(ESP) is been implemented. This ECU enables real-time data transmission, remote diagnostics, and predictive maintenance scheduling. optimized communication protocols and interfaces to ensure seamless integration with existing automotive infrastructure. The ESP technology with cloud integration ensures the safety of the vehicle by transmitting the real time data and by monitoring of this real time data the early faults can be detected. These findings underscore the potential of cloud technology in modernizing automotive safety and efficiency.

articleTitle: Massive MIMO Issues and Solutions- An Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The development of Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) is one of the key advancements for 5G and 6G networks. To simultaneously service a group of users' equipment, the base station contains an immense amount of antennas. An enhanced wireless technique is Massive MIMO, which communicates with several users at once by utilizing thousands of antennas at the base station. Greater data throughput along with higher capacity over conventional MIMO are the advantages of massive MIMO. There are some challenges associated with Massive MIMO. We will go over all the significant challenges that a system with massive MIMO faces, including estimation of channel, pilot contamination, precoding, user scheduling, energy efficiency, and signal identification, along with potential fixes. We also discuss the most recent development in massive MIMO networks for machine learning as well as deep learning.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Secure Medicine Supply Chain Using Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: From manufacture to distribution, the Internet of Things product life cycle is streamlined by supply chain management (SCM) control. Supply chain management requires blockchain integration to provide end-to-end monitoring, manufacturer-customer confidence, the eradication of fraud and counterfeit goods, and customisation of administrative expenses and documentation. The proposed project integrates blockchain and IoT technology to create a secure and transparent medical supply chain tracking system. RFID tags are affixed to medicine containers and sealed, ensuring authenticity from manufacturing to vendor delivery. At each checkpoint—manufacturing, dispatch, arrival, and vendor—the RFID tags are scanned, updating the location data on the blockchain. This process prevents the entry of counterfeit medicines into the supply chain. Vendors can verify the authenticity of the packages by scanning the RFID tags; a green light indicates authenticity, while a red light signals a counterfeit. The IoT components include NodeMCU, breadboard, and two lights for verification, an RFID tag and scanner etc providing real-time feedback during scanning. The blockchain ensures the integrity and security of medical data throughout the supply chain, enhancing trust and safety in the healthcare sector.

articleTitle: Early detection of sickness in cows using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The rising incidence of illnesses in cattle presents a noteworthy obstacle for the agricultural sector, affecting not only the well-being of animals but also the viability of the economy. In order to address this issue, the paper provides a comprehensive framework for diagnosis of cow illnesses that combines machine learning and deep learning (ML & DL) techniques. The novelty of this study specifically focuses on the four common diseases that affect cattle: mange, ringworm, cowpox, and lumpy skin disease. A sizable dataset for this study was created by gathering a variety of samples from different groups of cattle. Veterinary specialists carefully labeled each sample to guarantee correctness and dependability. The new composition of the dataset makes a substantial contribution to the progress of veterinary diagnostics research. Several algorithms are integrated in the proposed framework, such as Random Forest, Deep Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks, and Multilayer Perceptron (DNN, CNN & MLP). With the help of its special talents, each algorithm contributes differently to the disease diagnosis process by drawing useful patterns and features from the data. Additionally, with a 98 percent accuracy rate, the CNN model demonstrated its efficacy in identifying and differentiating between various cow diseases by collecting complex spatial information.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Predictive Maintenance in Distribution Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Distribution Transformers are an integral parts of the infrastructure which ensures reliable distribution of electricity in a city across various households. These transformers albeit robust are subject to various internal as well as external factors which may affect it’s working and increase reactive maintenance costs. The increasing complexity and criticality of power systems demand proactive measures for ensuring their reliable operation. Transformer faults represent a significant concern in power infrastructure, leading to downtime, financial losses, and potential safety hazards. This paper explores the application of machine learning techniques for the prediction of transformer faults, aiming to enhance the resilience and efficiency of power distribution systems. The proposed approach leverages advanced machine learning algorithms. By analyzing historical data from transformers, including oil levels, oil temperature, winding temperature, current and voltage levels the model learns patterns indicative of impending faults. The paper emphasizes the development of a predictive maintenance system that can identify potential transformer issues before they escalate, thereby minimizing downtime and reducing maintenance costs. A key component of the project includes model training using historical fault data. The research contributes to the broader field of predictive maintenance in power systems, demonstrating the effectiveness of machine learning in addressing critical infrastructure challenges. The outcomes of this project are expected to offer utilities and power system operators an invaluable tool for improving the reliability and longevity of transformers. Additionally, the integration of machine learning in fault prediction aligns with the industry’s shift towards smart grids and proactive maintenance strategies, contributing to a more sustainable and resilient energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Document Query Processing With Mistral 7B and Streamlit
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: PDF’s form an integral part in day to day life of every individual. Researchers, scientists, teachers and students need to read and go through tons of PDF in order to gain information. This is an overhead for the people. In past there have been multiple attempts to get the information from the PDF’s by directly asking the question. But most of the approaches are limited to single PDF and the accuracy is a concern with respect to the context in which answer is generated. In this paper we propose an approach that used Mistral 7B model to generate the answers to the questions asked by the user on multiple PDF’s uploaded at once. We also evaluate our model against the existing approaches to answer generation and demonstrate a better approach to solve the problem. Upon analysis we arrive at a conclusion that Mistral-7B outperforms other LLMs for this task. By incorporating prompt lookup technique, the response time was improved by approximately 80%.

articleTitle: Enhanced NTU by Modified Turbidity Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Turbidity of water is the measure of relative clarity of water. It is the cloudiness of water due to the presence of large number of suspended particles in water. To measure the turbidity of water in home appliances like dish washer and washing machine the standard available electronic turbidity sensor installed inside takes into account the light received by the phototransistor receiver from the light emitting diode in it. More the water turbid, more is the light scattered and lesser is the amount of light received by the receiver. The light gets scattered to all directions due to the suspended particles’ obstruction. The standard turbidity sensor used in such appliances use only the single phototransistor receiver to pick-up the un-scattered light. If we could measure the amount of the scattered light as well then we could get the enhanced realistic turbidity measurement of water. This paper proposes the simple, cost-effective modification in the existing available standard turbidity sensor to pick-up the light that is scattered due to the particles present in water with the help of additional receiver. This has proven to give the enhanced, realistic and better turbidity reading of turbid water. This modified turbidity sensor enables to account for the light scattered by the suspended particles in turbid water. The NTU (Nephelometric turbidity unit) turbidity sensors used commercially for real time water turbidity monitoring in lakes and rivers usually take into account the scattered light pick-up but are costly. This paper gives the cost-effective solution for the measurement of realistic turbidity of water in the form of simple modified turbidity sensor.

Author Keywords: simple cost effective NTU turbidity measurement

articleTitle: Student Performance Prediction Using AI-ML and Business Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: Portugal still trails behind in Europe despite improvements in recent decades in the educational level of its population. This is mostly because of Portugal's high rates of student failure, especially in basic subjects like Portuguese and Mathematics. Similar difficulties exist in India, where there is a chronically high percentage of student failure, particularly in science and math. This study uses business intelligence/data mining methodologies to address these problems by using real-world data, such as demographics, grades, and school-related aspects. In order to test four DM models and three input options, including prior grades, both nations use binary/five-level classification and regression tasks to model student performance. When past school period grades are taken into account, the results demonstrate increased prediction accuracy. The academic performance of students is subject to other factors outside their prior scores, including parental employment and education, alcohol consumption, and absenteeism. The findings of this study indicate the possibility of developing more effective techniques for predicting student outcomes, with the goal of improving the quality of education and optimizing the management of school resources.

articleTitle: Enhancing Support Vector Machine Prediction Accuracy for Global Solar Radiation Modeling Using Particulate Matter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: The amount of particulate matter in the surrounding can significantly affect the amount of incoming solar radiation. In this study, particulate matter [PM10 and PM2.5] is used as an additional input factor for a Support Vector Machine (SVM) model developed to calculate global solar radiation on the surface of the earth.
